text:
violet: heads up — the new sample app for Deno/Fresh is throwing a resolution error: "Cannot find package 'redwood-inference' subpath './client'" when importing `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference'`. Node + Vite bundles are fine. suspect exports/types mismatch. anyone familiar with typesVersions trick for deno?

jia: yep seen this. Deno expects explicit .js files and doesn't use Node's conditional resolution. two common approaches: publish a deno-ready entry (with .js ESM) or include an import_map for the app. publishing is nicer for a public SDK.

owen: can you paste the package.json exports + types bits? also are you using `.js` or `.mjs` in dist for ESM? Deno needs .js extension even if content is ESM.

violet: current package.json (trimmed):
```json
"main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
"module": "dist/esm/index.mjs",
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./client": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/client.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/client.js"
  }
},
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```

leo: two quick gotchas: 1) `.mjs` is fine for Node ESM, but Deno wants `.js` (and real MIME/Content-Type may also matter). 2) `types` is a top-level single pointer. You can't put types per-condition inside `exports` in a portable way. TS has `typesVersions` which can help consumers that use TypeScript to remap paths.

jia: exact. we've used `typesVersions` to point `redwood-inference/deno` imports to a separate d.ts bundle. Example in package.json: 
```json
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"typesVersions": {
  "*": {
    "deno": ["dist/deno/index.d.ts"],
    "deno/*": ["dist/deno/*.d.ts"]
  }
}
```
That maps TS imports like `import {X} from 'redwood-inference/deno'` to the deno types files.

owen: also consider adding an explicit export subpath "./deno" in `exports` pointing at `dist/deno/mod.js` (which re-exports existing ESM code but with .js extensions). Eg:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js" },
  "./client": { "import": "./dist/esm/client.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/client.js" },
  "./deno": "./dist/deno/mod.js"
}
```
That makes the deno import explicit: `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference/deno'`.

violet: ok that explains the runtime import issue. another problem: our auth module pulls in `node-abort-controller` polyfill + `node-fetch` and relies on `setTimeout` handles for backoffs. in some edge/deno environments fetch is global and AbortController exists, but the polyfills conflict and the token refresh timers seem to leak (timeouts never clear). any suggestions for runtime abstraction?

leo: prefer a tiny runtime adapter that picks implementations at build-time: e.g., `src/runtime/index.ts` exports an interface and then `src/runtime/node.ts` and `src/runtime/deno.ts` implement it. The bundler can be configured to resolve `src/runtime` to the correct implementation when building `dist/deno` vs `dist/esm`. For publishing, the deno bundle contains only deno-compatible code (no node-fetch).

jia: +1. Also avoid shipping node polyfills by default. For tiny SDKs we can detect environment at runtime via feature detection: `if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') use native; else use node-fetch`. But for deno builds it's safer to ship code that directly uses native APIs so tree-shaking doesn't pull node-only code into Deno builds.

nowen: typing edge case: our generated `.d.ts` files currently reference `./runtime` with extensionless imports: `import { X } from './runtime'`. That works in TS node resolution but in Deno TypeScript transpilation path those relative references confuse the import mapping if the published deno files use `mod.js`. we should emit deno d.ts files with `.js` in the module specifiers or use path-mapped typesVersions.

violet: so concrete plan you'd recommend?

leo: my suggestion:
- Add a `dist/deno` build that emits ESM .js files (mod.js, client.js) + matching `dist/deno/index.d.ts` with `.js` specifiers so Deno compiler is happy.
- Add "./deno" export in `exports` pointing to `dist/deno/mod.js` so user code can do `import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference/deno'`.
- Keep top-level `types` pointing to `dist/index.d.ts` (Node consumers) and add `typesVersions` mapping so TS consumers importing `redwood-inference/deno` pick up `dist/deno/index.d.ts` types.
- Remove node-only polyfills from the deno bundle and use runtime adapters.
- Add a tiny deno example in `examples/deno-fresh/` and a GH actions job that runs `deno cache` / `deno run --config tsconfig.json examples/deno-fresh/mod.ts` as an integration smoke test.

jia: I'll add lint rules to the build that fail if generated d.ts have extensionless imports for exported subpaths. helps catch this early.

build-bot: opened issue #4122: "SDK: add deno build + deno export subpath, typesVersions mapping, runtime adapter for fetch/AbortController, deno example + CI job" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4122 :rocket: 

violet: awesome. i'll put together a small PR that includes the minimal runtime adapter + deno build + docs update recommending `import from 'redwood-inference/deno'`. thanks all :sparkles: 

leo: small note for release: call out the deno entrypoint in changelog and examples — avoids support tickets like this one. :+1:
